many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

A prominent L-shaped component acts as a color marker. Find two separate monochrome objects with the same silhouette (translations; likely compare exact cell mask, and consider rotations/reflections only if needed). Recolor the one farther from the marker to the marker's color; leave the nearer copy unchanged. Distance appears to mean minimum grid/Manhattan distance between object cells, not center-to-center.

### Direct solved-instance evidence (task-ce4ada46)
Test grid had a large color-6 L at lower-left: horizontal arm row 15, cols 0–7, with vertical arm col 7 down to row 20. Two exact copies of a 7-cell mask existed:
- color 1, rows 5–8, cols 8–10: `100 / 111 / 110 / 100`
- color 8, rows 17–20, cols 0–2: `100 / 111 / 110 / 100`
The upper color-1 copy is much farther from the color-6 L marker than the lower-left color-8 copy. Recoloring the upper copy to 6 (and changing nothing else) was confirmed CORRECT.

### Supporting demo evidence
- Demo 1: color-1 L marker; two vertical dominoes (color 0 near marker, color 5 farther). Farther color-5 domino was recolored to 1.
- Demo 4: color-1 L marker; two same L-tetromino silhouettes (one color 0, one color 5); farther color-5 copy was recolored to 1.
- Demo 5: color-8 L marker; duplicate 10-cell irregular shapes (one color 2 lower-left, one color 4 upper-right); farther color-4 copy was recolored to 8.
These agree with “find duplicate silhouettes and recolor the more distant one to marker color.”

## Practical solving steps
1. Identify background (usually most frequent color) and connected foreground components (4-neighbor connectivity).
2. Locate the standout L-shaped/line-like marker component; its color is the output paint color. Ignore incidental same-color noise unless connected.
3. Normalize each other component to a binary mask after trimming its bounding box. Search for matching masks among different components (allow translated copies; rotations/reflections may plausibly count if no exact match).
4. For duplicate-shape candidates, compare each copy's minimum distance to marker cells. Recolor the farther copy entirely to marker color, preserving all other cells.
5. If multiple duplicated shapes, demos indicate the chosen pair may be determined by some further criterion; inspect all exact shape matches and use additional demos only when ambiguity remains. Do not assume the marker itself is necessarily a target duplicate.

## Important cautions
- The solved test supports this rule but not all task variants. Demo 2 was not fully explained during the attempt; do not overfit based on earlier speculative reasoning.
- One wrong submission in task-ce4ada46 was based on an incorrect guess changing a vertical color-5 pair near top-right; avoid that. The correct change was the full 7-cell repeated-shape object, recolored from 1 to 6.
- In the benchmark protocol, every action must end with exactly one JSON action object. Demo requests and wrong submissions each carry cost; use demos only to resolve material uncertainty.

# Continual-ARC pattern: colored object beside vertical divider

Observed task pattern (task-db2ffc1c, solved): a full-height vertical line of color 2 divides a uniform-background grid. A single irregular object (examples used colors 5, 6, and 7) lies on one side. Shift the object horizontally toward the color-2 divider until its bounding-box edge is immediately adjacent to the divider, preserving its exact row/column pattern and leaving its original area as background. Then draw a full-height color-8 line immediately on the object's other side (away from the divider), adjacent to its bounding box. If already adjacent to the divider, leave the object in place and put the 8-line immediately beyond its far edge. Preserve the divider, background, dimensions, and all object cells/holes.

Examples: in the 20x19 solved test, divider was column 13 (0-based); the 7-object moved to columns 9–12 and a full-height 8-line was placed in column 8. Demo 2 had divider column 14, object moved to columns 8–13, and line 8 at column 7. Demo 1 had divider column 12 and an object already at columns 13–14; object stayed and line 8 was placed at column 15.

Use only as a learned rule for matching future instances; verify against the actual grid geometry.

# Continual-ARC observations

## Task cb5c90a0: mirror-and-repeat grid

Verified by a correct submission on the 8x4 test grid and consistent with the 10x5 demonstration:

For an input grid of height H and width W, produce a grid of height 3H and width 2W.

1. For each source row `[a,b,...,z]`, make its horizontal mirror pair `[z,...,b,a,a,b,...,z]` (reverse the row, then append the original row).
2. Stack these transformed rows in three vertical blocks: input rows bottom-to-top, then top-to-bottom, then bottom-to-top. Equivalently, for output row-blocks use source row order `reversed(rows) + rows + reversed(rows)`.

This preserves all colors and gives dimensions `(3H) x (2W)`. Demo: 10x5 -> 30x10; test: 8x4 -> 24x8. This is an evidenced rule for this task family, not a universal ARC rule.
